answer:
Predicted probability of achieving efficacy PR at age 65 ≈ 0.395 (about 40%).

Primary model (pooled logistic regression, PR=1 vs SD/PD=0 across all 80 patients, Age the only predictor):
logit(P(PR)) = 4.4466 − 0.0750 × Age
- Age coefficient: −0.0750 (SE 0.0244, z = −3.08, p = 0.0021) — older age is significantly associated with lower odds of PR; odds ratio per year = 0.928.
- Model converged (5 iterations); fitted probabilities range 0.236–0.810, strictly inside (0,1), i.e., no separation in the pooled fit; McFadden pseudo-R² = 0.097, LLR p = 0.0011.
- Prediction: P(PR | Age = 65) = 1/(1+exp(−(4.4466 − 0.0750×65))) = 0.395 (95% Wald CI ≈ 0.27–0.53). Cross-checked by exact manual computation from the coefficients (0.395216).
- Empirical context: observed PR rate among the 23 patients aged 60–70 is 0.261, directionally consistent with the model's 0.395 at Age 65.

Sensitivity/evidence:
(a) Group × Efficacy crosstab (complete separation): Group 1 → 41 PR, 0 SD, 0 PD; Group 2 → 0 PR, 17 SD, 22 PD. Group membership perfectly determines efficacy.
(b) Arm-restricted Age-only logistic fits have no finite MLE: Group 1 (presumed treatment arm) has a constant outcome (all PR → probability → 1), and Group 2 has the opposite (no PR → probability → 0). No meaningful age-based prediction exists within a single arm, so the pooled fit is the primary candidate answer. No penalized/Firth fit was run, per instructions.

Caveats: (1) the file does not label which Group is the treatment arm — Group 1 is assumed to be treatment; (2) the primary prediction comes from a model pooling both arms, so it represents the age-associated probability of PR in this cohort, not an arm-conditional probability; (3) non-PR is defined as SD + PD (no CR level exists in the data). Analysis script retained at analysis/logit_age65.py; executed_analysis = true.
